root_idea.summary: The root develops from two related orientations: contact with earth or dust, and a route or means of departure.
root_idea.development: The dust image yields the notions of pressing the nose to the ground, abasement, compulsion, dislike, and frustrated inability to obtain one's due. A separate lexical branch gives مُرَاغَمٌ as a way, escape, or refuge to which one withdraws or emigrates.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form مُرَاغَمٌ; the Quran occurrence is an accusative, substantivized passive participle.

senses.definition: A way or means of departure, separation, or escape—a route by which one leaves or withdraws from an adverse situation.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction مُرَاغَمًا كَثِيرًا, this may be understood as a way to go elsewhere when one must distance oneself from wrongdoing or opposition; the departure can be framed as contrary to others' wishes.

senses.definition: A place of refuge or a destination to which one emigrates, flees, or transfers oneself; a secure retreat or stronghold.
senses.usage_conditions: The word can emphasize the place reached rather than the route taken. Classical interpretations of the Quranic passage include a fortified place.

senses.definition: A place or sphere in which one moves about while seeking the means of subsistence.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an interpretation of the same Quranic noun that emphasizes movement and livelihood-seeking rather than refuge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nose's cleaving or adhesion to earth or dust; also used in an imprecation wishing such abasement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may be understood literally or figuratively, with the figurative sense referring to humiliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abasement, humility, or submissiveness, especially submission imposed against one's will.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same branch is expressed verbally by رَغِمَ and أَرْغَمَ, and in Form II by imposing or causing abasement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be unable to obtain one's right or due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative extension of the image of the nose being pressed to the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To force or compel someone to do something against his will, including something he cannot refuse or resist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction can also describe doing something to another person against his will so as to vex or anger him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dislike, disapprove of, or hate something; to do something despite another's dislike or against his wishes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verbal noun occurs in expressions equivalent to “in spite of him” or “notwithstanding his objection.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Breaking off from, separating from, or abandoning someone in anger or hostility; becoming estranged or withdrawing from a group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may involve leaving one's people, cutting off friendly communion, or opposing them against their wishes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have no want, need, or requirement for something, and not to be unable to attain it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized usage of the Form III verbal expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cast something onto earth or dust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is used of throwing an object from the mouth or hand onto the ground, as well as of making a nose cleave to the dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To anger, vex, or wrong someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a causative or figurative use associated with imposing displeasure or abasement on another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become angry or angered, in speech or otherwise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participial description رَاغِمٌ may likewise mean angry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Earth, dust, or sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Authorities differ over whether the word most specifically denotes soft, fine, mixed, or non-flowing sand; it can also name a particular sandy tract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing that one desires, seeks, or hopes to obtain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is used of a sought-for object or advantage possessed or expected from another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The nose, or the nose together with the parts surrounding it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَرَاغِمُ is also used in this anatomical sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The accessory or appendage of the liver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This anatomical meaning is distinguished from the sense denoting the nose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The tubes or tube of the lungs, including the bronchial passage or windpipe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is attributed to some authorities and is distinct from the nasal and hepatic uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain plant, given as a dialectal variant of رُخَامَى.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a lexical plant name rather than an anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleeing or departing away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle also describes one who is abased, unable to obtain his due, angry, or disapproving, but those are separate uses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sheep or goat marked by whiteness or a differently colored patch at the tip of its nose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation concerns the animal's nasal coloration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain game of the Arabs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an independent traditional game name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who angers her husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an agentive, gender-specific lexical designation recorded as a specialized usage.

cautions: The single Quran occurrence is morphologically tagged as a passive participle but functions substantivally as a route or refuge noun.
Authorities differ over the precise texture and composition of رَغَامٌ; the entry therefore preserves the broader earth, dust, and sand sense.
